scope: Bounded supervisor-only repair of output emitted during timeout cleanup. Two tiny invented Linux subprocess stubs, standard library only. No historical imports, fixture construction, evaluator calls, games, real observations, external writes, or workflows.
execution_owner: Parent coordinator runs the combined finite suite; this worker does not execute tests.
prior_evidence: Preserve pre-sixth-repair-snapshot and all prior receipts, including the 180-test receipt, without rewriting history.

finite_cases.case: One stub installs a SIGTERM handler, prints a start line, and sleeps until a reduced cell-wall bound. The handler writes one short diagnostic line and exits zero. Require the original resource timeout cause, both output lines in order, observed/preserved byte equality, durable prefix, EOF-confirmed tail, no gap, and confirmed cleanup.

One stub prints a start line, then on SIGTERM writes a bounded burst exceeding a tiny helper output cap and exits zero. Require the original timeout primary outcome, exactly the capped output prefix, explicit resource overflow as a secondary failure, an output gap and unconfirmed tail when draining stops at the existing cap, and confirmed cleanup. No cap increase or additional cleanup deadline is permitted.

implementation_boundary: After process-group cleanup, nonblocking drain may consume only remaining time under the ORIGINAL absolute cleanup deadline and remaining bytes under the existing output allowance, with at most one extra observed byte to establish overflow. Mark EOF only after an actual empty read. Unobserved tail or discarded observed bytes must keep output_prefix_gap true even when the retained prefix is durable. No new resource budget, clock semantics, or scientific-record truncation.
